{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development and Hosting Agreement, HDI / the Company)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) | **Scope:** Playbook review of 18 rules | **Privileged & confidential**

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Three clauses sit at or above our preferred position and need no change (MFN, minimum commitments, employee non-solicitation). The remaining fifteen require action: **five core protections are entirely absent** and **nine clauses deviate from the fallback on material terms**, with one further item held for internal review.

The Agreement is skeletal on risk allocation. There is no indemnification or hold-harmless language anywhere, no limitation of liability (so both parties, including us, are exposed without cap and without an indirect/consequential damages waiver), no allocation of ownership in the Site, deliverables or our user, customer and transaction data, no vendor insurance covenant, no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, and no performance or conformance warranty from HDI beyond mutual corporate-authority representations in Section 9. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site on its own server and holds our Content and user data under Section 8.1, so these gaps sit squarely on the risks HDI creates.

At the same time, the commercial terms that do exist run against us. Section 4.2(a) imposes on the Company alone a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 in eight quarterly instalments — many multiples of our fallback cap of three months' fees, and capable of exceeding remaining contract value. Section 6.1 binds us to term-long exclusivity and an open-ended non-compete ("products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" and, "without limitation", named competitors "and companies similar to" them) with no performance exit, on a term that auto-renews annually under Section 4.1. Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited records inspection right; Section 10.3 leaves HDI free to assign the Agreement, including to a competitor named in Section 6, with no consent gate; Section 4.1 requires 90 days' notice to stop auto-renewal; Section 1.4 grants use rights to the Company alone with no affiliate path; and Section 10.5 selects New York law (our preference) but designates no forum at all.

Four issues are critical: the missing indemnity, the missing liability regime, the missing IP/data ownership allocation, and the Company-payable Termination Payment.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Our ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No clause; insert new § 9A (Art. 1–10 contain none) | HDI defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach and gross negligence/willful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation procedure and a narrow Company indemnity limited to Company-supplied Content and our own breach of law. Preferred (not fallback) targeted because there is no liability cap to super-cap. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | No clause; insert new § 5.5 (cf. §§ 1.1–1.3, 1.6, 2.1, 8.1) | HDI assigns the Site, Content, deliverables and work product to the Company; HDI retains pre-existing IP subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence for embedded HDI IP; Company retains all rights in user, customer and transaction data; no joint ownership. Fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify, sublicense) offered if HDI insists on platform title. |
| 3 | Critical | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 4.2(a) (cf. §§ 1.6, 3.1) | Delete the Termination Payment formula and state that no termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty is payable by the Company; 4.2(b)–(c) remain as mechanics with no amount to apply. Fallback: early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. |
| 4 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | No clause; insert new § 10.9 (Art. 10 runs 10.1–10.8) | Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees (tied to amounts payable by the Company under § 3) and USD 1,000,000; mutual waiver of indirect/consequential damages; uncapped Excluded Claims. Drafted at preferred level given genuine absence; placed in § 10, which survives two years under § 10.7. |
| 5 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 10.3 | Add Company affiliate/successor carve-out, consent (not unreasonably withheld) plus competitor bar on HDI assignment, and confirmation that a Company change of control gives HDI no termination right. Existing successors-and-assigns sentence preserved; mutual-notice fallback available. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (cf. §§ 4.1, 6.2, 9(b), 1.6) | Cap exclusivity at twelve months from the Effective Date and terminate it automatically on any HDI service-level or delivery-date failure (fallback position). HDI's reciprocal restriction in § 6.3 benefits us and is untouched. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 (cf. § 10.3) | Extend the § 1.4 access and use rights to Company affiliates identified by written notice (single sentence, fallback level). Successor coverage already met via § 10.3. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 6.1 (cf. §§ 4.1, 6.2, 9(b), 10.7) | Narrow the restriction to the named Deerskin Products, cap it at twelve months within the term, and carve out our internal development and acquisitions; HDI's "Deerskin" brand exclusivity for the Site left intact. § 6.3 binds HDI and is not flagged. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** (verification failed) | § 4.1; § 4.2(a) | Proposed: standalone Company right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice; HDI's convenience termination confined to end of term on 90 days' notice; Termination Payment capped at the lesser of the existing computation and three months of § 3.1 fees. **Redline not to be issued until re-drafted and re-verified.** |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 | Cap HDI's records inspection at once per year (single change to reach fallback). Notice (30 days), business-hours limit and HDI-borne costs already meet or better the playbook. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 10.5 | Keep New York law (our preference) and add one sentence giving the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction; the Agreement currently designates no forum. Not walk-away territory. |
| 12 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | No clause; insert new § 10.9 (Art. 10 ends at 10.8) | CGL $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate; E&O $2M; cyber and privacy $5M where HDI processes our Confidential Information or user data; statutory workers' compensation; certificates on request. Fallback: E&O $1M / cyber $2M. |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | §§ 1.8, 3.1–3.4, 7.1 | No change. The only parity covenant (§ 1.8) binds HDI in our favour. |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant (preferred) | §§ 3.1–3.3 (cf. §§ 4.2, 6.1) | No change. Pure revenue share on actual sales; the § 4.2 payment is assessed under the termination-fee rules, not double-flagged. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | No such covenant (cf. §§ 5.4, 6.1, 6.3, 10.2) | No change. If HDI proposes one, accept only the mutual, Services-limited, 12-month fallback shape with advertisement/unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation (redline repaired) | § 4.1 (cf. § 3.1) | Cut the Company's non-renewal notice window to 60 days (fallback) while leaving HDI's exit notice at 90 days for transition runway. No price-uplift mechanic exists, so that element is satisfied by inapplicability. |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | No clause; insert new § 4.3 (cf. §§ 1.4, 1.5, 1.3, 1.7, 8.1, 10.7) | Up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates; return of our Content, user information and transaction data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination; certified deletion thereafter. Fallback: 90 days' assistance with the same 30-day export. |
| 18 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 9 (insert new § 9(c); cf. §§ 1.6, 7.2) | Insert HDI performance and conformance warranty with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy; survives two years under § 10.7. Fallback accepted: 90 days software / 30 days Services with the same remedies. There is no existing disclaimer to carve out. |

**Roll-up:** 4 critical, 5 high, 9 medium. By status: 5 missing, 9 deviations, 3 compliant, 1 needs review.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings were assessed as walk-away territory (or at its boundary) under the applicable rule and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No indemnity at all (INDEMN, § 9A to be inserted).** HDI builds, hosts and operates the Site and provides the software and administration tools (§§ 1.1–1.5, 1.9), yet third-party IP infringement risk and unauthorised access to Content and user information on HDI's server sit with us with no recourse.
2. **Company-payable Termination Payment (LD, § 4.2(a)).** 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, uncapped, triggered by any Company termination including termination for HDI's own failure — many multiples of the fallback cap and capable of exceeding remaining contract value.
3. **Term-long exclusivity with no performance exit (EXCLUSIVITY, § 6.1).** Auto-renewal under § 4.1 means the restriction can run indefinitely; the only carve-outs are § 6.2 closeout merchandise and the § 9(b) Globix transition.
4. **Open-ended non-compete scope (NONCOMPETE, § 6.1).** "Substantially similar" products and named competitors "and companies similar to" them is the undefined scope the playbook treats as walk-away, with no internal-development or acquisition carve-out.
5. **Unlimited HDI inspection right (AUDIT, § 3.4).** Exercisable an unlimited number of times.
6. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE, § 10.9 to be inserted).** A hosting vendor that processes our data and user information (§ 8.1) with no coverage of any kind.
7. **No data return on exit (TRANSITION, § 4.3 to be inserted).** § 10.7 survival covers only §§ 6.3, 7, 9 and 10; on exit we would depend on HDI's goodwill for both continuity and recovery of our data.
8. **Licence limited to the Company alone (LICENSE, § 1.4).** Affiliates are excluded and § 10.3 closes the door entirely — assessed as edging into walk-away territory.
9. **90-day non-renewal notice (RENEWAL, § 4.1).** Above the 60-day fallback ceiling and at the walk-away boundary.

Related and equally material, though not labelled walk-away: the **complete absence of a liability regime** (LOL-CAP) and the **absence of any IP/data ownership allocation** (IP), both graded critical.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Hold the T4C redline.** Verification failed on finding f-t4c-cea91d19. We will re-draft the three operations (standalone Company convenience right; HDI convenience termination confined to end of term; "lesser of" cap at three months of § 3.1 fees) and re-run verification before anything goes to HDI. The commercial ask is sound; the drafting is not yet issuable.
2. **Resolve the section-numbering collision.** Both the limitation of liability (LOL-CAP) and the insurance covenant (INSURANCE) are drafted as a new **Section 10.9**. Renumber to 10.9 and 10.10 before the markup is circulated.
3. **Confirm the repaired RENEWAL edit.** The § 4.1 redline was auto-repaired; we will re-read it in context to confirm the Company's 60-day window and HDI's retained 90-day notice both read cleanly.
4. **Issue the markup in two tranches.** Tranche 1 (conditions of signature): INDEMN, IP, LOL-CAP, LD, INSURANCE, TRANSITION, WARRANTY, EXCLUSIVITY, NONCOMPETE, AUDIT. Tranche 2 (should-have, fallbacks pre-authorised): ASSIGN, LICENSE, GOVLAW, RENEWAL, and T4C once re-verified.
5. **Pre-clear the fallbacks with the business** so we can concede in one move: IP licence-back in lieu of assignment; three-month fee cap in lieu of deleting § 4.2(a); E&O $1M / cyber $2M insurance limits; 90 days' transition assistance; 90-day software / 30-day Services warranty; mutual-notice assignment in lieu of the competitor bar.
6. **Flag the two linked commercial points for the business owner:** the interaction between the § 4.2(a) Termination Payment and any exit under §§ 1.6 or 4.1, and the practical need for affiliate access under § 1.4.
7. **No action** on MFN, MINCOMMIT and NOSOLICIT — recorded as compliant at the preferred position; we will not raise them and will resist any HDI attempt to introduce a Customer-side MFN, volume commitment or non-solicit other than on the fallback shape noted above.
"}
